header.author: Latin curse tablets
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:defix:edh:noricum:lat, from the Epigraphic Database Heidelberg (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.21808.1.1: 21808: 'sivem' is taken as sive ('or'); the letters in braces ({no}, {I}) are superfluous and not translated. 'Caeserianus' may be a further name or a title (one of the emperor's household). 66874 reads as a dedication rather than a curse; n(umin--) leaves the number open, 'divine power' or 'powers'.

nodes.text: ve of the underworld, as you ought
of the underworld: summon now, more swiftly,
the one written below, and hand [him] over
nus's daughter, gives [this] at the bidding of the divine power.
